name: Barratt Impulsiveness Scale, Brief
construct: General trait impulsiveness measured as a unidimensional 8 item short form of the BIS-11 derived by item response theory.
licence: The article makes no availability or permission statement. The items are a subset of the freely distributed BIS-11 (Patton, Stanford and Barratt, 1995) and are listed in Table 3 of the article. The corresponding author is Lynne Steinberg (lsteinberg@uh.edu).

items.text: I act on the spur of the moment.

scoring: "The items are scored on a 4-point scale" and "total scores can be calculated by summing up the responses to the eight items" (range 8 to 32). Higher scores indicate greater impulsiveness. The article does not itself list reverse keyed items; the BIS-11 keying (impulsivity.org, Patton et al., 1995) reverse scores BIS-11 items 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 20, 29 and 30, which within the BIS-Brief are BIS-11 items 1, 8, 9 and 12 (BIS-Brief items 1, 4, 5 and 6 here). Items 5 and 9 (BIS-11 numbering) were treated as a testlet in the IRT analysis but both contribute to the summed score. No published cut offs.
citation: Steinberg, L., Sharp, C., Stanford, M. S., & Tharp, A. T. (2013). New tricks for an old measure: The development of the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale–Brief (BIS-Brief). Psychological Assessment, 25(1), 216–226. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0030550
transcriptionNote: Item text transcribed from Table 3 of the article (Graded Model Item Parameter Estimates for the Eight BIS-11 Items); the table gives BIS-11 item numbers only, so items are renumbered 1 to 8 here with the original BIS-11 number in each item note. Item 3 keeps the article's typographic quotation marks around "pay attention." The article gives no respondent instructions, so the instructions field is empty; the BIS-11 instructions were not retrieved. Response option labels and values are from the article; reverse keying is from the BIS-11 scoring key at https://www.impulsivity.org/measurement/bis11, not from the BIS-Brief article.
